data.title: Bexarotene (oral + topical gel)
data.summary: Retinoids · Third-generation retinoid (rexinoid) — selective RXR agonist
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Retinoids_

**Class:** Third-generation retinoid (rexinoid) — selective RXR agonist

## Mechanism of action
- Binds retinoid X receptors → induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation of malignant T cells

## Pharmacokinetics
- Take with a fatty meal; metabolised by CYP3A4

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Oral: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (mycosis fungoides) refractory to at least one systemic therapy (approved)
- 1% gel: early-stage (IA/IB) mycosis fungoides lesions (approved)
- Off-label gel: hand eczema, lymphomatoid papulosis, alopecia areata

## Dose & formulations
- Oral: 300 mg/m²/day (start at 100–150 mg/m² and increase)
- Gel 1%: every other day at first, increasing up to 2–4 times daily as tolerated

## Adverse effects
- Central hypothyroidism (almost universal — suppresses TSH) → levothyroxine needed
- Severe hypertriglyceridaemia (risk of pancreatitis) → fibrate/statin often started with it (avoid gemfibrozil — raises bexarotene levels)
- Leucopenia, headache, mucocutaneous dryness, photosensitivity
- Gel: irritant dermatitis, pruritus

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (teratogenic); pancreatitis risk; uncontrolled lipids

## Drug interactions
- Gemfibrozil and CYP3A4 inhibitors raise levels; reduces efficacy of hormonal contraceptives

## Monitoring
- Fasting lipids weekly at start, free T4 (not TSH), CBC, LFT

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (category X); two contraceptive methods (one non-hormonal).

## Viva points
- RXR-selective 'rexinoid'
- Central hypothyroidism — monitor free T4
- Hypertriglyceridaemia — avoid gemfibrozil

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.22 and ch.37; Khopkar (Retinoids; topical retinoids). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
